# TODO Calculate PSD and POC flux for the 2021 and 2023 data
This uses the _PAR_Aggregated files from Ecopart.

The methods explained in Rufas et al. 2025 adapting the Bisson et al. 2022 approach of the truncated power law. Additionally, a MC Error propagation can be applied to account for the uncertainty in the sampling volume simular to Rufas et al. 2025.

Note that seasonal variation in POC flux is expected based on the results in the Rufas et al. 2025 aggregation (i.e., decrease in flux post-bloom).

Note that in the truncated power law model in Bisson et al. (2022), the modelled particle count is lower for larger particles (stronger decrease with higher lambda).

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# UVP Data processing
Following the matlab scripts in the Rufas et al. (2024) paper.
https://github.com/annarufas/Rufas_etal_2024_GRL/blob/master/code/processPocFluxFromUvp.m

## Establish the size class bins and bin width
Note that the last size class is >16.4 mm but set the max bin to 32.768mm. This size bin seldom has any observations so can be discarded later.
```{r}
# 
UVP6_sizebins_edges_um <- c(1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768)
N_sizebins <- 15

# Convert um to mm
UVP6_sizebins_edges_mm <- UVP6_sizebins_edges_um * 0.001
# Get width of size bins
UVP6_sizebins_width <- UVP6_sizebins_edges_mm[1:15]
# Get midpoints of size bins
UVP6_sizebins_mid <- UVP6_sizebins_edges_mm[1:15] + UVP6_sizebins_width/2 


```

## Functions for calculating and modeling the POC flux at each depth
The PSD is based on the LPM (large particulate material) concentrations (# L-1) by size classes.
- In the calculatePocFlux function: the psd and binMiddle inputs are arrays for each depth bin. The zeros are not removed since these are summed anyway.
- In the calculateModelledPsd: observedVol is a single value, and observedN/binWidth/binMiddle are arrays
```{r}
# Function modified from Rufas_etal_2024_GRL/code/processPocFluxFromUVP.m
# The value returned has units of:  mg C m-2 d-1
calculatePOCFlux <- function(psd, binMiddle) {
  # Input:
  #   psd, # part L-1
  #   binMiddle, mm
  # 
  # Output:
  #   pocFlux, mg C m-2 d-1
  
  particleRadius <- (binMiddle / ((4/3) * pi))^(1/3)
  particleEsd <- particleRadius * 2

  # Flux factor function from Eq. 5 in Bisson et al. (2022)
  fluxFactor <- function(d) 2.8 * d^2.24

  pocFlux <- sum(psd * fluxFactor(particleEsd), na.rm = TRUE)

  return(pocFlux)
}

# For the truncated power law method in Bisson et al. (2022)
# NOTE observedN is the concentration * volume sampled

# library(stats)
calculateModelledPsd <- function(observedN, observedVol, binWidth, binMiddle) {
  # Modelled particle number (# part./um), Eq. 1 in Bisson et al. (2022)
  modelledN <- function(x, d) {
    x[1] * d^-x[2] * exp(-d / x[3])
  }
  
  # log10 transform observedN and divide by bin width
  observedN_log10 <- log10(observedN / binWidth)
  observedN_log10 <- unlist(observedN_log10)
  
  # Only consider populated size classes and remove the ones that are not
  bad <- which(is.infinite(observedN_log10))
  observedN_log10_good <- observedN_log10[-bad]
  binMiddle_good <- binMiddle[-bad]
  
  # Initial guess and bounds for model parameters
  # PP: Originally, x0 is c(40, 4, 0.1) but I changed it to c(10, 4, 0.1) to remove the error "Error in optim(par = x0, fn = function(x) { :  L-BFGS-B needs finite values of 'fn'"
  #       C1    alpha lambda
  x0 <- c(10, 4, 0.1) # # part L-1 / unitless / mm
  lower <- c(-Inf, 0, min(binMiddle_good))
  upper <- c(Inf, 6, max(binMiddle_good))
  
  # PP: In the original code, this is the fminsearchbnd() Matlab function.
  # Optimise model parameters using optim with box constraints (L-BFGS-B)
  opt <- stats::optim(
    par = x0,
    fn = function(x) {
      sum((observedN_log10_good - log10(modelledN(x, binMiddle_good)))^2)
    },
    method = "L-BFGS-B", 
    lower = lower,
    upper = upper
  )
  
  C1 <- opt$par[1]
  alpha <- opt$par[2]
  lambda <- opt$par[3]
  
  estimNbl <- (modelledN(opt$par, binMiddle) / observedVol) * binWidth
  
  # Remove particle size classes that are not in the observed set
  estimNbl[bad] <- NA
  
  list(estimNbl = estimNbl, C1 = C1, alpha = alpha, lambda = lambda)
}

generateRandomSamplesOfParticleNumber <- function(observedNbl, observedVol, 
                                                  nIterations = 100, 
                                                  N_sizebins = 15) {
  # Assume observedNbl follows a negative binomial distribution and draw nIterations 
  # samples from it to obtain simulatedN
  
  simulatedN <- matrix(NA, nrow = nIterations, ncol = N_sizebins)
  simulatedNbl <- matrix(NA, nrow = nIterations, ncol = N_sizebins)
  
  for (iSc in 1:N_sizebins) {
    if (observedNbl[iSc] > 0) {
      size_param <- as.numeric(observedNbl[iSc] + 1/2)
      prob_param <- 1 / (observedVol + 1)
      simulatedN[, iSc] <- rnbinom(nIterations, size = size_param, prob = prob_param)
      simulatedNbl[, iSc] <- simulatedN[, iSc] / observedVol
    }
  }
  
  return(simulatedNbl)
}


# Test random sampler
simulatedNbl <- generateRandomSamplesOfParticleNumber(a_par, a_vol)

fluxIter <- rep(NA, nIterations)
for (iIter in seq_len(nIterations)) {
  if (sum(simulatedNbl[iIter, ], na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
    fluxIter[iIter] <- calculatePOCFlux(simulatedNbl[iIter, ], UVP6_sizebins_mid)
  }
}
fluxErr <- sd(fluxIter, na.rm = TRUE)


# Test
depth_i <- 50 # the depth bin to analyze
a_par <- ecopart_2021_5[depth_i,7:21]
a_vol <- ecopart_2021_5$Sampled_volume_L[depth_i]
a_binm <- UVP6_sizebins_mid
a_binw <- UVP6_sizebins_width

# What if no <100um like UVP5 ---> an order of magnitude lower!
a_par2 <- a_par
a_par2[6:7] <- 0

# No modelling
calculatePOCFlux(a_par, a_binm)
calculatePOCFlux(a_par2, a_binm)

# With truncated power law model
observedN <- round( a_par * a_vol )
trunc <- calculateModelledPsd(observedN, a_vol, a_binw, a_binm )
calculatePOCFlux(trunc$estimNbl, a_binm)
```

### For testing the random sampler simulated particle concencrations
```{r, eval=FAKSE}
df_simulated <- data.frame(
  ESD = rep(UVP6_sizebins_mid, times = 10),
  ParticleNumber = as.vector(t(simulatedNbl[1:10, ])),
  Group = rep(1:10, each = length(UVP6_sizebins_mid))
)

df_observed <- data.frame(
  ESD = UVP6_sizebins_mid,
  ParticleNumber = as.numeric(a_par) * a_vol
)

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = df_simulated, aes(x = ESD, y = ParticleNumber, group = Group), color = "black") +
  geom_line(data = df_observed, aes(x = ESD, y = ParticleNumber), size = 1.5, color = "blue") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "ESD (mm)", y = "Particle number") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Calculate POC flux
```{r}
# For each row apply the calculations
# TODO should the 32-128 um size classes be removed to match UVP5 measurements?
pocFlux <- A %>% 
  select(sample_id, Depth_5m, Sampled_volume_L)

# TODO generalize later to just do the entire ecopart df with all stations
for (i in c(1:nrow(pocFlux))) {
  a_par <- A[i, 7:21]
  a_vol <- A$Sampled_volume_L[i]
  
  # No model
  pocFlux$ObsFlux[i] <- calculatePOCFlux(a_par, UVP6_sizebins_mid)
  # With truncated power law model
  observedN <- round( a_par * a_vol )
  trunc <- calculateModelledPsd(observedN, a_vol, 
                                UVP6_sizebins_width, UVP6_sizebins_mid )
  
  pocFlux$ModelFlux[i] <- calculatePOCFlux(trunc$estimNbl, a_binm)
  pocFlux$C1[i] <- trunc$C1
  pocFlux$alpha[i] <- trunc$alpha
  pocFlux$lambda[i] <- trunc$lambda
  
  # Add the random samples function for sample volume error
  simulatedNbl <- generateRandomSamplesOfParticleNumber(a_par, a_vol)
  fluxIter <- rep(NA, nIterations)
  for (iIter in seq_len(nIterations)) {
    if (sum(simulatedNbl[iIter, ], na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
      fluxIter[iIter] <- calculatePOCFlux(simulatedNbl[iIter, ], UVP6_sizebins_mid)
    }
  }
  pocFlux$fluxErr[i] <- sd(fluxIter, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Start at 128 um size class?
  a_par128 <- a_par
  a_par128[1:7] <- 0
  pocFlux$ObsFlux128[i] <- calculatePOCFlux(a_par128, UVP6_sizebins_mid)
  observedN <- round( a_par128 * a_vol )
  trunc <- calculateModelledPsd(observedN, a_vol, 
                                UVP6_sizebins_width, UVP6_sizebins_mid )
  pocFlux$ModelFlux128[i] <- calculatePOCFlux(trunc$estimNbl, a_binm)
  
  
  # Add the random samples function for sample volume error
  simulatedNbl <- generateRandomSamplesOfParticleNumber(a_par128, a_vol)
  fluxIter <- rep(NA, nIterations)
  for (iIter in seq_len(nIterations)) {
    if (sum(simulatedNbl[iIter, ], na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
      fluxIter[iIter] <- calculatePOCFlux(simulatedNbl[iIter, ], UVP6_sizebins_mid)
    }
  }
  pocFlux$fluxErr128[i] <- sd(fluxIter, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Observed vs modelled flux
cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(pocFlux, aes(x = ObsFlux, y = Depth_5m)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_point(aes(x = ModelFlux), color = "blue") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ModelFlux - fluxErr, 
                      xmax = ModelFlux + fluxErr), width = 0, color = "blue") +
    scale_y_reverse(),
  
  ggplot(pocFlux, aes(y = Depth_5m)) +
    geom_point(aes(x = ModelFlux128), color = "deepskyblue") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ModelFlux128 - fluxErr128, 
                      xmax = ModelFlux128 + fluxErr128), 
                  width = 0, color = "deepskyblue") +
    geom_point(aes(x = ObsFlux128), color = "pink") +
    scale_y_reverse() 
)

# The Modelled POC flux + error bar
ggplot(pocFlux, aes(x = ModelFlux, y = Depth_5m)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ModelFlux - fluxErr, 
                    xmax = ModelFlux + fluxErr), width = 0, color = "blue") +
  scale_y_reverse()
```
